title: Insects Gone in a Century
passage: Insects Gone in a Century. In the past, humans had to be scared of insects in order to avoid bites. However, in modern life, there's no need to fear insects. For one, we rarely come into contact with dangerous insects. Secondly, insects are very important to nature. One job of insects is to help us lower the amount of food waste, and another is to pollinate. Insects help fruits to grow, as well as other important foods we feed to animals whose meat we later eat. In fact, it has been reported that insects are responsible for 30% of everything we eat. Despite this, more than 40% of all bug types may be gone within the next 100 years. Insects like bees and butterflies are dying out because of humans, and clearly, this is a problem. We have taken away their homes to create new farms and cities. We have also caused pollution and serious changes in the weather. Insects everywhere are disappearing eight times faster than other animals, and by killing them, we may be killing ourselves.
